evidence.note: Mutation test: reverted the hunk to `defer file.Close()` in a scratchpad copy of the tree and ran golangci-lint run ./internal/sessionhistory/... -- it goes red with `internal/sessionhistory/sessionhistory.go:224:18: Error return value of file.Close is not checked (errcheck)`. Restoring the branch version lints clean (0 issues). The change is a real fix for a real finding, not decoration.

Claim check on the new comment ("Read-only path: there is nothing a Close error could tell the caller"): the handle comes from os.Open at line 220, which is O_RDONLY, and it is the only file open in the whole file. No writes are buffered behind this descriptor, so a Close error cannot signal lost data; every read error is already surfaced through scanner.Err() at line 236. The comment asserts a property the code actually has.

Behavioural equivalence verified: `file` is assigned once at line 220 and never reassigned, so wrapping the call in a closure (late binding) cannot select a different receiver than the old `defer file.Close()` (early binding). The early `return` inside the scan loop at line 232 still runs the deferred close. No leak, no semantic change.

Coverage: go test ./internal/sessionhistory/... -coverprofile shows block 225.17,225.35 (the new closure body) with hit count 1, and readJSONLSignal at 87.5%. The added statement is executed by the existing suite, so the closure does not introduce an uncovered statement or move the package coverage floor down. Package tests pass (ok, 0.285s).

The lint config claims "nothing is excluded: the noisy cases were fixed at the source instead". This hunk is consistent with that claim -- errcheck is left enabled and the call site is corrected, rather than the rule being disabled or the function added to an exclude list.

Consistency check across the duplicated pattern: the identical `// Read-only path...` comment plus `defer func() { _ = file.Close() }()` appears at epicsource.go:84, state.go:62, runchain.go:110, reviewlog.go:286, findings.go:484 and tasksource.go:61 -- and every one of those is an os.Open (O_RDONLY) site. The rationale is not misapplied to any write handle, and no read-only close site in the tree was left with the old bare form (grep for `defer <x>.Close()` in non-test Go code returns zero hits).

Counter-check on the write paths: record.go:189 (O_RDWR|O_APPEND) and machine/sidecar.go:95 do NOT carry the read-only rationale; record.go instead documents that the append ends in f.Sync so the row is durable before Close runs. The distinction between read and write justifications is drawn correctly, so the read-only wording in this shard is not a blanket excuse pasted over sites where a Close error would matter.
